reasoning:
**What is asked.** Whether Donald Trump's approval in the Silver Bulletin average falls, on any day from 16 to 31 December 2026, strictly below every earlier value of his second term. The bar is the lowest value up to 15 December, so a new low set before then raises the hurdle. It resolves on the tracker's data file in early January.

**Starting point.** The record low is 36.3%, set shortly before the 3 November midterms. The average then recovered to about 38% and has turned down again: 37.8% on 9 November and 37.6% on 12 November (Newsweek), and 37% approve, 60% disapprove on 17 November, when the tracker's own note called the rating "back on the downswing". It sits about 0.8 points above the record, with four weeks before the window opens.

**Base rate.** The slide has been steady: 39.7% on 30 March, 38.3% on 21 May, 37.6% on 23 September, 36.3% in late October, roughly 0.3 to 0.5 points a month, with new lows in at least five separate months this year. But each low was followed by a partial rebound, and here the lowest point must fall inside 16 particular days.

**Recent evidence.** Individual polls are flat at low levels rather than still falling: Reuters/Ipsos has shown 32% in four straight polls (latest 13 to 16 November), Economist/YouGov had 32% (9 to 11 November), and the New York Times average is 36%, equal to its low. Government funding runs out on 11 December (NerdWallet, 13 November); a shutdown would add downside, though leaders of both parties back a stopgap. Fewer polls appear over the holidays, which damps movement inside the window.

**How I combined it.** Simulating the average as a noisy series starting near 37.1% gives about 27% with no trend, 40% with a decline of 0.3 points a month and 50% with 0.5 points a month. I weight these roughly 45/25/30 and add a little for the shutdown risk.

**What makes it No.** A trough before 16 December followed by a bounce, or a rating that simply holds near 37%.

**Forecast.** 38%.
